talks.title: Even the AI Guy Couldn't Find the Chat Button
talks.details: Treat AI as a collaborator, not a vending machine: ask it to interview you before it builds a lesson plan, log what actually happens after you use its output, and benchmark any fix before trusting it.

event.name: Shree Niketan Schools — Teachers' AI Q&A

talks.title: How to Build AI Products — and Prove They Work
talks.details: Build AI products around evidence, not ideas: prototype quickly, test with agents and real users, and iterate until the product proves its value.

event.name: SUTD DAI Signature Master Class · Expert Industry Series

talks.location: Singapore University of Technology and Design, Singapore

talks.title: What's Left For Us
talks.details: As AI takes over production, human value shifts to judgment, context, and verification. The real bottleneck is the cost of checking AI's work.

talks.title: You Don't Even Need to Code
talks.details: Coding is becoming specification and review: describe the outcome, let agents build it, and focus on whether the result works.

talks.title: Why Are You Even Sitting in This Class?
talks.details: AI can generate charts and analysis. The enduring skill is knowing what deserves to be visualized, challenged, and communicated.
talks.location: Department of Engineering Design, IIT Madras, Chennai

talks.title: What Is This Course Really Teaching?
talks.details: Tools change faster than curricula. The course is really about learning how to learn, automate work, and judge results rather than memorizing tools.

talks.title: How Do You Manage Something Smarter Than You?
talks.details: Managing AI resembles managing experts: specify work clearly, verify outputs systematically, and borrow proven practices from professions that already manage complex judgment.

talks.title: Hire a Data Scientist for $100
talks.details: Agentic tools can perform much of a data scientist's research and analysis cheaply. The leverage comes from framing the question and checking the result.

talks.title: Invite AI to the Table

event.name: AI in Education — Sivaswamy Iyer School

talks.details: Teachers should use AI as a participant in lesson planning, explanation, assessment, and reflection—not treat it as a separate subject or shortcut.

talks.title: When Data is for Agents, Not Humans
talks.details: Data increasingly serves agents rather than dashboards. Structure it so agents can research, analyze, benchmark, and act reliably on behalf of people.

talks.title: The Curator's Dilemma
talks.details: When AI makes charts abundant, curation—not production—becomes scarce: deciding what deserves attention, what is trustworthy, and what fits the audience.

talks.title: Free Methods, Priced Judgment
talks.details: AI makes sophisticated analytical methods cheap and accessible. The scarce skill becomes choosing the right analysis, questioning assumptions, and judging whether results matter.

talks.title: The Workshop That Made Itself
talks.details: AI can design and execute workflows while a session is running. The useful skill is orchestrating tools, context, and verification rather than following a fixed script.

talks.title: The Data Stack for an Agentic World
talks.details: Data stacks should be designed for agents, not dashboards: expose granular data and judgment-rich context so agents can aggregate and reason for each question.

talks.title: Data Stories with AI
talks.details: AI can turn raw data into analyses, narratives, visuals, and alternative explanations. The craft shifts to questioning, verification, and editorial judgment.

talks.title: Let AI Take Your Exams
talks.details: If AI can pass an exam, the exam may be measuring the wrong thing. Assessments should reward effective AI use, verification, and real-world outcomes.

talks.title: The Moving Boundary
talks.details: AI keeps moving the boundary between disciplines and automation. Education should organize around problems and judgment rather than fixed departmental skill boxes.

talks.title: What Your AI Doesn't Know About You
talks.details: AI performance depends less on clever prompts than on context. Give models the right goals, examples, constraints, history, and tools so they can act effectively.

talks.title: Agents are the New Software
talks.details: Software is shifting from fixed interfaces and workflows to agents that interpret goals and choose actions dynamically. Products should be designed around delegated outcomes.

talks.title: Inventing the Future of Learning
talks.details: AI breaks the old link between learning, producing work, and proving competence. Education must redesign practice and assessment around what humans should still learn and demonstrate.

event.name: Harvard Graduate School of Education panel

talks.title: The Dinner Table Theory of AI Skills
talks.details: AI makes traditional signals of competence easy to fake. Skills and assessments should focus on valuable questions, validation, accountability, and outcomes AI cannot certify for us.

talks.title: A Thousand Professors In Your Pocket
talks.details: Everyone now has access to an endlessly patient expert. The opportunity is to use AI as a tutor and thinking partner while building habits for checking its mistakes.

talks.title: Innovation as a Frontier
talks.details: Innovation is frontier exploration, not a pipeline with a known destination. Leaders should fund cheap experiments, learn quickly, and expand what becomes possible.

images.label: AI-generated Hack of the Day cards

talks.title: The Journalist and the Machine
talks.details: Journalists can use AI to turn curiosity into rapid experiments and explainers. The machine accelerates research and production; editorial judgment decides what is worth publishing.

talks.title: The McKinsey in Your Pocket
talks.details: AI gives individuals on-demand access to research, analysis, and structured advice once reserved for expert teams. Institutions should redesign work around that new leverage.

talks.title: Design in the Age of Infinite Generativity
talks.details: When AI can generate endless options, design shifts from making artifacts to choosing constraints, framing problems, and deciding what should exist.

images.label: Leave the math to the machines

talks.title: Verification Architecture for Autonomous AI
talks.details: Autonomous agents are useful only when their actions can be trusted. Constrain workflows, verify intermediate outputs, and design explicit checks before granting autonomy.

talks.title: AI for IITM Office of Institutional Advancement

event.name: Office of Institutional Advancement, IIT Madras

talks.details: AI can automate research, outreach, personalization, and analysis in institutional advancement. The largest gains come from redesigning workflows rather than adding a chatbot.

talks.title: The Open-Book Exam We Never Designed
talks.details: When every student has a powerful AI tutor and solver, conventional closed-book assumptions collapse. Assessments must measure judgment, verification, and application instead.

talks.title: AI in SDLC — Panel Discussion
talks.details: AI is entering every stage of software development. Teams need to redesign the SDLC around faster generation, stronger automated checks, and human accountability.

talks.title: How Students Learn Python
talks.details: Students increasingly learn Python by asking AI, copying examples, and debugging interactively. Teaching should embrace these paths while preserving conceptual understanding and verification.

talks.title: AI Roadmap for Engineering Education
talks.details: Engineering education should treat AI as infrastructure across the curriculum, not a standalone elective. Courses, assessment, and faculty workflows all need redesign.

talks.title: Vibe Coding for Humanities
talks.details: Coding agents let humanities students build software without becoming programmers. The valuable skill is expressing intent clearly and critically evaluating what the machine produces.

talks.title: Your Chotu Is Smarter Than You Think
talks.details: Modern AI is capable enough to handle surprisingly broad knowledge work. Treat it like a smart junior colleague: delegate aggressively, then review where it matters.

talks.title: Agentic AI in Action
talks.details: Agents turn LLMs from answer generators into workers that use tools, execute multi-step tasks, and recover from failures. The challenge is control and verification.

talks.title: Applied Vibe Coding
talks.details: Vibe coding treats code as a disposable build artifact. Specify the outcome, let agents implement it, and spend your effort reviewing behavior rather than typing code.

talks.title: Mining Digital Exhaust
talks.details: Everyday digital traces—chats, logs, histories, submissions—contain valuable signals. LLMs make it practical to mine them for patterns, stories, and decisions.

talks.title: Data to Decisions with AI
talks.details: LLMs can automate expensive clinical-data work from protocol checks to anomaly detection and enrollment analysis, provided verification is designed into the workflow.

talks.title: Vibe Analytics
talks.details: Vibe analysis lets AI handle code and analytical mechanics while you focus on useful questions, surprising insights, verification, and what action follows.

talks.title: Applied Vibe Coding
talks.details: With coding agents, specifications become the product and code becomes cheap. Work faster by delegating implementation, testing aggressively, and optimizing for review.

talks.title: LLM Psychology
talks.details: LLM psychology treats models as minds to probe: test how prompts, personalities, costs, and failure modes change behavior, then use evidence to choose and manage them.

talks.title: LLM Data Visualization

event.name: IIT Madras — Department of Engineering Design

talks.details: LLMs can generate, interpret, and even invent visualizations. The analyst's role shifts toward asking better questions, testing novelty, and judging whether a visual is useful.

talks.title: Vibe Coding
talks.details: Vibe coding focuses on outcomes rather than code. Give agents clear requirements and enough context, let them implement, and judge delivered behavior instead of implementation details.

talks.title: Vibe Analysis
talks.details: Vibe analysis delegates the analytical process to agents and focuses humans on business outcomes. Explore broadly, verify key claims, and automate successful analyses afterward.

talks.title: LLM Trends
talks.details: LLMs are becoming cheaper, smarter, longer-context, more autonomous, and more multimodal at once. Each trend makes previously bespoke workflows practical to automate.

talks.title: LLMs: Ask me anything
talks.details: AI is becoming cheap, capable infrastructure. Use it heavily, manage it like a large team of smart interns, and build verification into the work.

talks.title: Vibe Analysis
talks.details: Vibe analysis uses LLM agents across the full data workflow while humans stay pragmatic and skeptical: seek useful outcomes, challenge them, and publish reproducible work.

talks.title: LLMs: Ask me anything
talks.details: AI capability is improving far faster than organizational adoption. Use it now, focus on practical outcomes, and expect culture, trust, and workflow redesign to be harder than technology.

talks.title: DuckDB is the new Pandas
talks.details: DuckDB offers a simpler, faster analytical default than Pandas for many workloads: SQL, low memory use, remote files, rich functions, and embedded deployment.

talks.title: AI Coding Guide
talks.details: AI coding works best when repositories are easy for agents to understand, tasks are well-scoped, tests are fast, and humans review outcomes rather than keystrokes.

talks.title: RIP Data Scientists
talks.details: Almost every task a data scientist does today can be automated using LLMs. The role of data scientists must change.

talks.title: Social Code Analysis
talks.details: Code can be analyzed socially, not just technically: repository behavior, collaboration patterns, and AI-based evaluation reveal how people build software and where process breaks.

talks.title: Cool LLM CLI Python uses — with agents
talks.details: LLM command-line workflows can automate everyday Python tasks, then grow into agents that execute code and perform reliable calculations with tools like Pydantic AI.

talks.title: Solving Industrial Problems with Live Coding

event.name: AWS Innovation Day — Manufacturing, Industrial and Supply Chain

talks.details: LLMs can turn messy industrial and IoT data into working analyses live, collapsing the gap between domain question, code, model, and decision.

talks.title: Goodbye MBA, Hello AI
talks.details: AI is a foundational shift for managers: analytical and production work gets cheaper, so advantage moves to problem selection, judgment, communication, and organizational change.

talks.title: Prompt-to-Plot
talks.details: LLMs can move from a natural-language question to data, analysis, and a finished visualization. The challenge is specifying intent and validating the resulting chart.

talks.title: Data Design by Dialogue
talks.details: Data visualization can become a dialogue with AI: explore alternative charts, critique them, and iterate conversationally until the design communicates the right idea.

talks.title: Cool LLM CLI Python uses
talks.details: LLM command-line tools make Python automation conversational: inspect files, transform data, call APIs, and compose workflows by describing the result you want.

talks.title: Python in the Browser
talks.details: Modern browsers can run substantial Python locally, making interactive tools easier to distribute: many applications need no server, installation, or backend.

talks.title: Vibe Coding
talks.details: Vibe coding lets people build software by describing what they want and iterating on results, even if they do not understand or inspect the generated code.

talks.title: How to use AI to generate code?
talks.details: AI can generate useful software from plain-language instructions. Start with small outcomes, iterate on failures, and treat generated code as something to test rather than trust.

talks.title: AI as a learning tool: What students, teachers, and parents need to know
talks.details: AI can personalize explanation, practice, and feedback for students and teachers, but effective use depends on critical thinking, ethics, and checking what the system produces.

talks.title: Finding Actor Look-alikes
talks.details: Multimodal embeddings can turn faces into searchable vectors, making it possible to find visually similar actors across large image collections with surprisingly little custom machine learning.

talks.title: LLM Psychology
talks.details: Language models exhibit measurable behavioral tendencies that resemble personality. Treating them like subjects of psychological experiments reveals which prompts and models work best.

talks.title: Finding Actor Look-alikes
talks.details: Multimodal embeddings can turn faces into searchable vectors, making it possible to find visually similar actors across large image collections with surprisingly little custom machine learning.

talks.title: Automating Comics
talks.details: Data and code can automate much of comic creation—from selecting scenes and dialogue to layout—turning storytelling rules into reproducible software.

talks.title: Prisoners of Birth
talks.details: Where we are born strongly shapes education, income, health, and opportunity. Data visualization makes the scale of this inherited inequality visible.

talks.title: Visualizing Data Anomalies
talks.details: Anomalies are often the most valuable part of a dataset. Visual exploration helps distinguish errors, rare events, and patterns that conventional summaries hide.

talks.title: Visualizing Politics
talks.details: Political data becomes more understandable when visualized at human scale. Maps and charts can expose voting patterns, representation, and anomalies that tables conceal.

talks.title: NCERT NRG Workshop
talks.details: A practical workshop on using data and visualization to explore educational questions, turning raw information into patterns that are easier to understand and discuss.

talks.title: Python Imaging
talks.details: Python can automate image processing tasks such as transformation, measurement, composition, and batch manipulation, making visual workflows programmable and reproducible.

talks.title: Learning R
talks.details: An introduction to using R for data analysis: importing and manipulating data, running statistical analyses, and creating reproducible visualizations.

Frontiers in Technology
talks.details: Government leaders need to anticipate frontier technologies years before they mainstream. Today's policy, R&D, and capability investments determine whether India leads or catches up.

talks.title: True but Irrelevant
talks.details: Rigid schemas can be technically correct yet operationally irrelevant. Preserve provenance, annotate assertions separately, and model the data people actually produce.

talks.title: AI First Thinking for HR Professionals
talks.details: AI-first HR means redesigning work, not adding a chatbot. Better questions, structured context, process re-engineering, and AI as a first-class participant matter more.

talks.title: Making Open Data Useful: Lessons from Diagram Chasing
talks.details: Open data is useful only when people can find, understand, trust, and reuse it. Good interfaces, validation, documentation, and reproducible pipelines turn publication into utility.

talks.title: Building a culture of openness
talks.details: Open peer review can turn conference selection into community learning. Clear roles, public feedback, scoped incentives, and measurable outcomes make openness sustainable.

talks.title: Homelabbing with Bare Metal
talks.details: Homelabbing works best when hardware is low-power, modular, and easy to reconfigure. Iterative DIY rigs make experimentation cheap enough to follow curiosity.

talks.title: The Accomplished Beginner
talks.details: A portfolio career requires becoming an accomplished beginner again and again: experiment with one foot, combine disciplines, and use past accomplishments as confidence rather than status.

talks.title: The Glass Wall of Class
talks.details: Class divides make other people's choices look irrational because their context is invisible. Crossing the glass wall builds empathy and reveals shared human motives.
